story.title: Investigation Reopened into Alleged 2024 Cornell Fraternity Rape Case
story.summary: Prosecutors in New York are reopening an investigation into an alleged gang rape that occurred at a Cornell University fraternity in 2024. This decision follows a civil lawsuit filed by the alleged victim against seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity, claiming she was drugged and raped at their house.

explore_lenses.label: Why was the 2024 case reopened now?
explore_lenses.title: A new lawsuit triggered a fresh review
explore_lenses.summary: The reopening follows a September 2026 civil complaint that described allegations prosecutors say differed sharply from the 2024 statement they had reviewed. The district attorney says the renewed review will test whether newly available evidence changes the earlier charging decision.

claims.text: The civil complaint was filed in New York Supreme Court on September 16, 2026, naming Cornell, Chi Phi-related entities, seven students, a bar and other defendants; its allegations are not court findings.

District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said the 2024 sworn statement provided to his office described drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious and consensual, unlike the later civil complaint's allegations.
Doe's attorney, Thomas Giuffra, disputes the DA's account of the earlier response, saying authorities received group-chat material and failed to conduct adequate follow-up with his client.

explore_lenses.label: Why does Cornell's response matter?
explore_lenses.title: Campus discipline and criminal law are separate
explore_lenses.summary: The case concerns two distinct processes: the prosecutor's decision on criminal charges and Cornell's internal Title IX/student-conduct process. Cornell says its process ended with expulsions and suspensions, while the plaintiff's lawsuit seeks to establish institutional and individual civil liability.

claims.text: Cornell said its internal investigation and hearing process resulted in a range of sanctions, including expulsions and suspensions, and that the Xi chapter of Chi Phi remains barred from campus.
Cornell says federal student-privacy law prevents it from publicly identifying individual disciplinary outcomes; it rejects the claim that those involved faced only minimal consequences.

The civil complaint requests a jury trial and asserts claims including negligence, breach of contract, state human-rights and education-law violations, sexual assault, sexual battery and a Dram Shop Act claim against the bar.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the criminal case?
explore_lenses.title: Prosecutors plan a grand-jury presentation
explore_lenses.summary: The DA has said he intends to present the matter to a Tompkins County grand jury with Doe's cooperation, after reassessing evidence and potential charges. That announced step is not an indictment, and the accused have not been criminally charged as of September 28, 2026.

claims.text: Van Houten said his office would reexamine whether additional evidence unknown in November 2024 could support a finding of criminal conduct and that he intends to present the case to a Tompkins County grand jury.
A grand-jury presentation may result in no indictment, an indictment of some people, or indictments of all people prosecutors choose to present; the DA has not announced charges.

At least two named defendants have publicly disputed the allegations: Scott Kretzschmar's lawyer said he did not assault or touch Doe, and Scott Norris said he did not participate in sexual activity or drug use.

story_report.summary: Tompkins County prosecutors are reopening an investigation into an alleged gang rape at Cornell University in 2024 after the alleged victim filed a civil lawsuit against seven fraternity members. District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said his office will review whether additional evidence unknown in November 2024 could support criminal findings and plans to present the matter to a grand jury. No criminal charges have been announced.

sections.heading: Civil Complaint Names Cornell Defendants
sections.body: The civil complaint, filed in New York Supreme Court on Sept. 16, 2026, names Cornell, Chi Phi-related entities, seven students, a bar and other defendants. It seeks a jury trial and includes claims alleging negligence, breach of contract, state human-rights and education-law violations, sexual assault, sexual battery and a Dram Shop Act violation against the bar. The allegations in the complaint have not been adjudicated and are not court findings.

sections.heading: Accounts of Earlier Investigation Differ
sections.body: Van Houten said a sworn statement provided to his office in 2024 described drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious and consensual, differing from allegations in the later lawsuit. The alleged victim's attorney, Thomas Giuffra, disputes that account, saying authorities received group-chat material and did not adequately follow up with his client. Two named defendants have also publicly denied key allegations: Scott Kretzschmar's lawyer said he did not assault or touch Doe, while Scott Norris said he did not participate in sexual activity or drug use.

sections.heading: Cornell Reports Discipline and Chapter Ban
sections.body: Cornell said its internal investigation and hearing process resulted in sanctions ranging from suspensions to expulsions, and that the Xi chapter of Chi Phi remains barred from campus. The university said federal student-privacy law prevents it from identifying individual disciplinary outcomes and rejected the assertion that those involved faced only minimal consequences.

unresolved.text: It is not publicly resolved what evidence prosecutors had in 2024, what evidence is newly available, or whether the differing accounts can be reconciled.

No timetable has been announced for grand-jury action or a charging decision. A grand-jury presentation could produce no indictment, indictments of some people, or indictments of all people prosecutors present; criminal guilt and civil liability have not been determined.

related_stories.title: Russian Drone Strikes Kyiv Science Academy and Hospital, Causing Casualties
related_stories.summary: A Russian drone strike hit the National Academy of Sciences in central Kyiv, resulting in at least one death and multiple injuries. The attack caused significant damage to the historic building, with flames visible as people attempted to escape. This incident is part of a broader pattern of drone strikes targeting Ukraine's capital, which has seen increasing violence in recent days.
